description.en:
Kill the ocean.
Every Iberian who yearns to join the Inquisition carries that resolution to some degree, and so do I. But I can only murmur it in my heart, for I hold no rapier—only a spade for planting sugarcane. In every coastal village and town across Iberia, there must be people who share my thoughts. Some joined the Punitive Force; others died. This town is remote; an Inquisitor only comes once every two years on patrol to recruit newcomers. It was that time of year again, but evidently they were late, or perhaps they wouldn't come at all. I've seen the horrors of the Seaborn, and I knew what joining the Punitive Force meant. Yet I needed a real weapon—like an Inquisitor's rapier. I prayed that strength would free me from my terror of the sea, and breathe life back into this forgotten town.
A stranger arrived in town. Not an Inquisitor, but a petite Liberi looking for lodging. She dressed dashingly and bore a lengthy name, seemingly of noble descent. Every day she gave speeches in the square, drawing large crowds whose laughter and wonder echoed all the way to the shore. I cared nothing for her origins; my eyes were fixed on the blade at her hip—a proper weapon, capable of combating the Seaborn and the tides, capable of truly letting someone accomplish something. Sadly, it wasn't mine to wield.
The crowd behind that noble grew larger, gesturing and planning all across town. Getting the mayor's approval took her some effort. I couldn't understand why she didn't simply brandish her blade—was it merely an ornament? The chance to find out came soon enough. The noble stepped into my field, tasting the irrigation water and inspecting the withered sugarcane. If she wished to purchase the land, I would gladly part with it; so long as I could join the Inquisition afterwards, I would never return to this desolate town. Hearing my words, she drew her blade—looking every bit the conquistador now—thrust the fine weapon into the earth, pulled it back out, rubbed the soil on the tip between her fingers, and proposed a trade.
"You want to collateralize your blade for my shovel?"
"That's right, just for a moment."
The noble plunged the shovel into the earth and twisted it—as expected, she was unsuited for farm work, looking utterly clumsy. Yet, the sand slowly darkened, and water began seeping up from beneath, pooling in the pit like a miniature sea.
"There's freshwater underground not far from your field. Connect it to Rhodes Island's irrigation system, and it will keep your bellies full for the coming year. A descendant of the Iberian Royal Navy, the great Lady De Toledo, gives you her word."
"A navy descendant... using a shovel? Farming sugarcane?"
"You care about that? I'm fulfilling my 'noblesse oblige'! Besides, I tried digging with my blade, and it was terribly inefficient. As for you, standing here watching the sea with a shovel every day, did it never cross your mind to dig downward?"
I looked at the field at my feet and the noble blade planted in the dirt, forgetting for a moment the Inquisition and the roaring sea. The noble calling herself De Toledo said she would stay in town, inviting me to join the irrigation team. Perhaps once the sugarcane ripens, I can ask to borrow that blade to peel some stalks.
description.zh:
杀死大海。
渴望加入审判庭的伊比利亚人或多或少会怀抱着这样的决心，我也是。但我只能在心里如此默念，因为我的手里没有刺剑，只有一把种甘蔗的铁锹。伊比利亚沿海的每一座村镇里，应该都有跟我想法相似的人，他们中的一部分加入了惩戒军的队伍，一部分死去。这座镇子偏僻，审判官两年才会来巡视一次招募新人。今年也到了这个时候，但显然他们来晚了，或者不会再来了。我见过恐鱼的惊悚之处，知道加入惩戒军的后果，但我需要一柄真正的武器——比如审判庭的刺剑，我祈祷力量会让我不再畏惧大海，也会复兴这座被遗忘的镇子。
镇子里来了个陌生人，不是审判官，是个借宿的小个子黎博利。她穿得很威风，名字很长，似乎是哪个贵族的后代。她每天都在广场上讲演，很多人去听，笑声和惊叹声传到海边都不散。我不关心她的来历，我看到的是她腰间的佩刀——一把正儿八经的武器，可以对抗恐鱼和浪潮，可以真的让人做到点什么。可惜，它不在我的手上。
那名贵族身后的人越来越多，他们在镇上各个地方比比划划。获取镇长的批准花了她一些力气，我不明白她为什么不直接亮出自己的佩刀，难道那只是装饰品吗？验证的机会很快就来了，那名贵族走进我的田地，尝了尝用于灌溉的水和枯萎的甘蔗。她如果想要收购这片土地，我求之不得，只要之后能加入审判庭我就不会再回到这个荒芜的镇子。她听了我的话，拔出佩刀——现在她确实像一位征服者——随后将那柄漂亮的武器插进地里，又抽了出来，用手捻了捻刀尖的土粒，向我提出了一项交易。
“您想用佩刀抵押，换我的铁锹？”
“没错，就借一会儿。”
贵族将铁锹插进地里转动——果然她不适合干农活，看上去很费力。不过，沙土的颜色渐渐变深，水从地下渗出，在土坑里像一小片海。
“离你田地不远处的地下就有淡水，接上罗德岛的灌溉系统，可以让你们在接下来的一年里吃饱肚子。伊比利亚王家海军后裔，伟大的德·托莱多大人向你保证。”
“海军后裔……用铁锹？种甘蔗？”
“你在意这个？我可是在实行我的‘贵族义务’！而且我试过用佩刀挖土，效率实在太低了。倒是你，每天拿着铁锹来这个地方看海，从来没想过往地下挖挖？”
我看着脚下的田地和插在地里的贵族佩刀，一时间遗忘了审判庭和喧嚣的大海。自称德·托莱多的贵族说自己会在镇上留下，她邀请我加入灌溉系统的搭建小组。或许等到甘蔗成熟之后，我可以问她借这柄刀削甘蔗。
